facts.label: Increased risk with H. pylori infection

visuals.title: Where the late signs appear
visuals.text: Virchow's node in the left supraclavicular fossa, Krukenberg tumours in both ovaries, Sister Mary Joseph nodules at the umbilicus.

visual.caption: Air under the diaphragm (pneumoperitoneum) after gastric perforation.

visuals.title: From red flag to stage
nodes: Weight loss, upper abdominal pain or age >55

glossary.Malignancy: A cancer: abnormal cells that grow uncontrollably and can invade and spread.
glossary.Histological: Relating to the microscopic appearance of tissue.
glossary.Histology: Examining tissue under a microscope to see what cells are present.
glossary.Gastric mucosa: The inner lining of the stomach.
glossary.Hypertrophy: Enlargement of a tissue because its cells grow bigger.
glossary.Chronic gastritis: Long-standing inflammation of the stomach lining.
glossary.Epigastric: The upper central abdomen, just below the breastbone.
glossary.Metastases: Secondary tumours formed when cancer spreads from where it started.
glossary.Perforation: A hole through the full thickness of an organ wall.
glossary.Peritonitis: Inflammation of the peritoneum, the lining of the abdominal cavity, often from spilled gut contents.
glossary.Diaphragm: The dome-shaped muscle separating the chest from the abdomen.
glossary.Biopsy: A small sample of tissue taken for examination under the microscope.
glossary.Endoscopy: Looking inside the gut with a flexible camera tube.
glossary.Staging: Working out how big a cancer is and how far it has spread.
glossary.Gastroduodenal anastomosis: A surgical join between the remaining stomach and the duodenum.
glossary.Anastomosis: A join between two tubes, such as bowel or blood vessels.
glossary.Resection: Surgical removal of part or all of an organ.
glossary.Partial gastrectomy: Surgical removal of part of the stomach.
glossary.Endoscopic stenting: Placing a mesh tube through a blocked segment using an endoscope to keep it open.
glossary.Metastatic: Cancer that has spread to distant sites.
glossary.Prognosis: The likely outcome of a disease.
glossary.Lymphatic spread: Cancer cells travelling through lymph vessels to lymph nodes.
glossary.Supraclavicular fossa: The hollow just above the collarbone.
glossary.Infiltrates: Spreads diffusely through tissue rather than forming a lump.
glossary.Locally advanced: Cancer that has grown into nearby tissue or nodes but not spread distantly.
glossary.Chemotherapy: Drugs that kill rapidly dividing cancer cells.
glossary.Precursor: A condition that comes before, and can turn into, another (here cancer).
glossary.Metaplasia: Change of one mature cell type into another, usually in response to chronic irritation.
glossary.Lymph nodes: Small filters along lymph vessels that trap cells and microbes and can harbour cancer spread.
